carbohydrate-calculator.assumptionNote: Macro targets are starting points, not medical advice. People with diabetes or kidney disease should get personalised targets from a clinician or dietitian.
benefits: Turns a vague 'eat fewer carbs' into an exact daily gram target.
Shows the healthy 45-65% range so you can see where any diet sits.
Helps athletes fuel training with enough carbohydrate.
Makes food labels meaningful: compare grams per serving against your target.

faqs.a: They are the body's preferred fuel, especially for the brain and high-intensity exercise. Your body can also run on fat and protein, but carbs are the cheapest, fastest energy source.
About 130 g per day is the minimum the brain needs from glucose, which is why very low-carb diets force the body to make ketones instead. Most guidelines suggest 45-65% of calories.
faqs.q: How many carbs do I need minimum?

faqs.a: Yes, very-low-carb and keto diets sit at 10% or less of calories. They work for some people but need planning for fibre, electrolytes and sustainability. Check with a clinician first.
One cup of cooked rice is about 45 g of carbs, a medium roti about 15 g, a banana about 27 g, and a slice of bread about 14 g. Weighing food for a week teaches portions fast.
faqs.q: How many carbs are in common foods?

faqs.a: It usually takes 2-4 days of very low carb intake to enter ketosis, where the liver makes ketones from fat. It is not the goal of ordinary low-carb eating.
Whole carbs (oats, lentils, brown rice, fruit) come with fibre and nutrients that slow digestion. Refined carbs (sugar, white flour) spike blood sugar faster and satisfy less.
faqs.q: Do whole carbs differ from refined carbs?

carbohydrate-calculator.formula:
Carb grams = daily calories x carb % / 100 / 4.
Carbs provide 4 kcal per gram.
AMDR healthy range: 45-65% of calories. Minimum for the brain: about 130 g/day.
howTo: Enter your daily calorie target (use the TDEE calculator if you do not know it).
Pick a diet style: balanced, high-carb, low-carb or very low.
Read your daily carb target in grams, the healthy 45-65% range, and the 130 g minimum.
Compare food labels against your target when planning meals.
keyFacts: Carbohydrates provide 4 kcal per gram, the same as protein and less than fat's 9 kcal.
The accepted healthy range (AMDR) is 45-65% of daily calories from carbs.
The brain alone needs about 130 g of glucose per day.
Fibre is a carbohydrate that is not digested; it feeds gut bacteria and steadies blood sugar.
Whole carbs like lentils, oats and fruit come with fibre and micronutrients.
A 2,200 kcal balanced diet at 50% carbs means 275 g of carbs per day.

carbohydrate-calculator.quickAnswer: Daily carbs come from your calories times your carb share, divided by 4 kcal per gram. On a 2,200 kcal balanced diet at 50% carbs, the target is 275 g per day, inside the healthy range of 248-358 g. The brain needs a minimum of about 130 g per day.
carbohydrate-calculator.tagline: Find your daily carb target in grams - balanced, high-carb, low-carb or very low.
carbohydrate-calculator.workedExample:
2,200 kcal, balanced diet (50%):
1. Calories from carbs = 2,200 x 50 / 100 = 1,100 kcal.
2. Grams = 1,100 / 4 = 275 g/day.
3. Healthy range: 2,200 x 45% / 4 = 248 g up to 2,200 x 65% / 4 = 358 g.
4. 275 g sits inside the healthy range and well above the 130 g minimum.
